title: 2026-10-22_Linux_NyaDrop_Backdoor_Investigation_909
description: Investigate and respond to a Linux/NyaDrop backdoor malware infection on an IoT device network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder for a company that manages a network of MIPS-based IoT devices. Recent network monitoring has detected suspicious outbound connections from one of the devices. Your task is to investigate this activity, identify the source of the infection, and take appropriate action to contain and remove the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) via SSH using the provided credentials. Username: investigator, Password: Investigator123!
levels.local_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) via SSH using the provided credentials. Username: investigator, Password: Investigator123!

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the network, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the target host. Investigate the target host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running on the system.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, you can use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services. Look for any services that seem out of place or unfamiliar. The suspicious service in this scenario is `nyadrop.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the list of running services and look for any that seem out of place or unfamiliar.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: You have identified a suspicious service running on the target host. Determine how this service is automatically started after reboot.
levels.solution: To identify the persistence mechanism, you can use the command `systemctl list-unit-files --type=service` to list all systemd service unit files. Look for any services related to the suspicious service. The suspicious service in this scenario is started by the `nyadrop.service` systemd unit.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate the systemd services and timers to find any related to the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-unit-files --type=service` to list all systemd service unit files.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: The suspicious service appears to be communicating with an external command-and-control server. Determine which network port is used for this communication.
levels.solution: To identify the network port used for communication, you can use the command `ss -tulnp` to list all listening network ports. Look for any ports that seem suspicious. The suspicious service in this scenario is using port 4444 for communication.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the network connections and listen ports to find the one used by the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to list all listening network ports.
